subject: Stability safeguard decision for OrthoAI deployment / SLA alignment
messages:

Cc: Priya Dalal <priya.dalal@orthoai.com>

Subject: Re: SLA question + rollout guarantees for initial go-live

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looked great for our test set. Before we sign the SOW we'd like to confirm how Redwood will handle progressive releases in production. Our legal team requires a 99.95% uptime commitment for inference in the clinician-facing flows, and they asked how rollout policies (canaries / A-B) are used to mitigate risk. Specifically: 1) can we require an automatic revert to a pinned stable model if latency or 5xx rate exceeds thresholds, and 2) can you guarantee a pinned rollback that takes <30s to execute?

We are also evaluating whether to run on Dedicated pools or Hosted — please flag any differences to SLA behavior.

- Samir
Head of Engineering, OrthoAI

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Priya Dalal <priya.dalal@orthoai.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA question + rollout guarantees for initial go-live

Samir — thanks, great questions. Short answer: yes, and we can formalize an exception path in the SOW to meet the <30s rollback window you asked for when on Dedicated. Longer answer below.

Proposal (high-level):
- Deployment pattern: staged A/B (10% canary, 30% stagger, 60% steady) with an automated "circuit-breaker" monitor.
- Automatic fallback: if error-rate or p99 latency breaches configured SLOs for 2 consecutive sampling windows (1 min windows), traffic is routed back to the last pinned stable hash. The routing change is orchestrated by the control plane and applied at the edge; for Dedicated customers we push the change at the routing layer and it is sub-30s in tests.
- Pinning: we maintain immutable model hashes. On a canary start we create a pinned safe-hash of the previous production model. Auto-revert uses that pinned hash.
- Manual override: SRE on-call can pin a version and hold traffic while debug occurs.
- Telemetry / safety gates: per-route telemetry (5xx, lat p99, token throughput) and a short-term canary playback test to detect regressions that don't surface in standard metrics (e.g., hallucination score delta).

Attached is a compact proposal doc and a draft SLA-exception form to include in the SOW. If you want, we can tighten thresholds or shorten the sampling window for your flows.

Jordan Blake
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Stability safeguard decision for OrthoAI deployment / SLA alignment

Looping in Marcus for the Dedicated capacity / infra cost bits. Quick notes on failure modes and cost:

Failure modes where auto-revert may not immediately restore latency:
- Model-side regressions: if the new model increases average per-token compute (longer decode loops), reverting helps but transient cache/replenishment artifacts can take a minute to settle.
- Cache warming: reverting to a pinned model may require KV-cache repopulation; we mitigate this by pre-warming the pinned instance during the canary window.
- Downstream network flaps or node-level OOMs: routing to the pinned hash won't help if the underlying pool has degraded — in Dedicated we provide isolated pools, reducing this risk.

Costs: keeping a pinned instance warm for fast rollback — we can offer a "warm standby" option: a small reserved slice (shared across pinned versions) to ensure sub-30s switchover. For Dedicated customers this is negligible compared to the pool commit; for Hosted we can provide it as an add-on (approx +8% on peak inference commit). We'll add exact numbers to the SOW.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Product, Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-13T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stability safeguard decision for OrthoAI deployment / SLA alignment

Samir / Priya — approving the exception path for OR-3492 to include:
- a pinned safe-hash rollback with control-plane routing that targets <30s in Dedicated testing;
- warm-standby reservation for the first 72h post-go-live (no additional charge for first 72h as a one-time onboarding concession);
- a requirement that customer accept a 2-min standby telemetry window for auto-reverts (we tested 1 min but for safety we'll standardize on 2 consecutive 60s windows for this deal).

I'll ask legal/procurement to sign off on the SLA wording and include the exact thresholds in Attachment B of the SOW. Jordan / Grace — please confirm the finalized thresholds and I will route the internal approval.

Marcus Lin
VP, Cloud Operations — Redwood Inference
